mainEntity.name: Can I sell your SEO audit as my own product?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The audit can carry your branding and be sold on its own or used as the start of a retainer.

mainEntity.name: Do you do link building too?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, as a separate service. See our white-label link building page for how outreach and placements are handled.

mainEntity.name: Can you promise rankings for my client?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and you should not either. Rankings depend on many factors. We commit to the work in the scope and report what moves.

mainEntity.name: Will my client know MMC is involved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you choose to tell them. We sign an NDA, work under your brand, send deliverables in your format and do not contact your clients unless you ask us to.

acceptedAnswer.text: We start with the client's site, analytics and search console access, sign the NDA and run an audit. You then get a plan to present.

cta.lede: On a call, with a senior strategist. We scope your first SEO client and agree how we work behind you.

stages.breaks: Access arrives late, so the audit starts blind.
stages.why: Without Search Console and CMS access, findings are guesses and the fix list slips past the client call.
stages.does: One access checklist goes out at the start, and we log what is missing so the audit scope stays honest.

stages.breaks: Keywords are mapped to pages nobody agreed.
stages.why: If you and the client have not signed off the map, every later page is open to argument.
stages.does: We group searches by intent, map each to a page and send the map for your approval before any writing.

stages.breaks: Thin pages ship to hit the deadline.
stages.why: A rushed page with nothing new on it will not rank, and the client blames the agency.
stages.does: Briefs say what each page must add, and a second editor checks it against the brief before it reaches you.

stages.breaks: Pages bury the answer the buyer came for.
stages.why: Search results and AI answers favour pages that reply first and explain after.
stages.does: Priority pages are reopened with a direct answer, then detail, FAQs and matching structured data.

stages.why: A traffic chart does not tell the client whether SEO paid for itself.
stages.does: Your report pairs rankings and traffic with enquiries from the client's own analytics, plus a plain next-steps note.
